title: Composition comparison for restricted module transport and its left adjoints
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], and let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$, $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ be lax monoidal functors, with tensor maps $\mu^P,\mu^Q,\mu^H$. Give $QP$ its composite lax structure. Let $c:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ be a monoidal natural isomorphism, and let $A,B,C$ be monoid objects of $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$, respectively [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Suppose given morphisms of monoid objects
$$\psi:B\to PA,\qquad\chi:C\to QB,\qquad\varphi:C\to HA,\qquad\varphi=c_A\circ Q(\psi)\circ\chi.$$
Using module objects, transport and scalar restriction [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-modobj-transport, def-sfb-modobj-restriction], put
$$T_P=\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}\operatorname{mapMod}(P),\quad T_Q=\operatorname{Res}_{\chi}\operatorname{mapMod}(Q),\quad T_H=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\operatorname{mapMod}(H).$$
For every $A$-module $M$, write $a_M,b_M$ for the $C$-actions on $T_QT_PM$ and $T_HM$. They are
$$a_M=Q\bigl(P(\gamma_M)\circ\mu^P_{A,M}\circ(\psi\otimes1_{PM})\bigr)\circ\mu^Q_{B,PM}\circ(\chi\otimes1_{QPM}),\qquad b_M=H(\gamma_M)\circ\mu^H_{A,M}\circ(\varphi\otimes1_{HM}).$$
Assume that every $c_M$ is $C$-linear from $T_QT_PM$ to $T_HM$:
$$c_M\circ a_M=b_M\circ(1_C\otimes c_M).$$
Then $c_M^{-1}\circ b_M=a_M\circ(1_C\otimes c_M^{-1})$, for every $A$-linear $t:M\to N$ one has $H(t)\circ c_M=c_N\circ QP(t)$, and there is a unique natural isomorphism $\delta:T_QT_P\xrightarrow{\sim}T_H$ whose component and inverse on underlying objects are $c_M$ and $c_M^{-1}$.
Suppose in addition that adjunctions $S_P\dashv T_P$, $S_Q\dashv T_Q$, $S_H\dashv T_H$ are given. Let $u_1$ be the unit of $S_H\dashv T_H$ and $u_2$ the unit of the composite adjunction $S_PS_Q\dashv T_QT_P$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. There is a unique natural isomorphism $d:S_H\xrightarrow{\sim}S_PS_Q$ satisfying, for every $C$-module $M$,
$$T_H(d_M)\circ u_{1,M}=\delta_{S_PS_QM}\circ u_{2,M}.$$
Its conjugate is $\delta$ under these adjunctions, and the conjugate of $d^{-1}$ is $\delta^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. No invertibility is required of $\psi,\chi,\varphi$; only $c$ is required to be an isomorphism.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-modobj-transport], transporting an action along $P$ replaces $\gamma_M$ by $P(\gamma_M)\circ\mu^P_{A,M}$, and transporting a module map $t$ gives $P(t)$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], restricting along $\psi$ precomposes this action with $\psi\otimes1$ and leaves the underlying objects and maps unchanged. Repeat these two substitutions with $Q,\chi$, and do the single substitution with $H,\varphi$. They give exactly the displayed $a_M,b_M$, and the underlying maps of $T_QT_P(t)$ and $T_H(t)$ are $QP(t)$ and $H(t)$. The monoid-morphism hypotheses on the three coefficient maps are precisely those needed for these restrictions.

source.place: pushforward-composition sentence; unfold the transport and restriction actions

proof.text:
Fix $M$. Compose the assumed equation $c_M\circ a_M=b_M\circ(1_C\otimes c_M)$ on the left with $c_M^{-1}$ and on the right with $1_C\otimes c_M^{-1}$. The bifunctor laws of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and $c_Mc_M^{-1}=1$ give
$$a_M\circ(1_C\otimes c_M^{-1})=c_M^{-1}\circ b_M.$$
Thus $c_M^{-1}$ is $C$-linear by the morphism criterion in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. The forward map is linear by hypothesis, and their two composites are identity module maps because their underlying composites are identities and a module morphism is just an underlying morphism satisfying the action equation.

source.place: pushforward-composition sentence; invert the stipulated linear component

proof.text: For an $A$-linear map $t:M\to N$, naturality of the given natural isomorphism $c:QP\cong H$ is $H(t)\circ c_M=c_N\circ QP(t)$. With the underlying maps identified in step 1, this is precisely the naturality equation for the module isomorphisms of step 2. Explicitly, multiplication by $c_N^{-1}$ on the left and $c_M^{-1}$ on the right gives $QP(t)\circ c_M^{-1}=c_N^{-1}\circ H(t)$, so the inverse components are natural as well. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] equality and composition of module morphisms are those of their underlying maps; hence these components define $\delta$ and its inverse. Any other natural isomorphism with the prescribed underlying components has the same module morphisms at every object, proving uniqueness.

source.place: pushforward-composition sentence; naturality and uniqueness of the lifted comparison

proof.text: Suppose the three adjunctions are given. Form $S_PS_Q\dashv T_QT_P$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], applying first $S_Q\dashv T_Q$ and then $S_P\dashv T_P$; its unit is the specified $u_2$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with source category $\Mod_C(\mathcal E)$, target category $\Mod_A(\mathcal C)$, $(L_1,R_1)=(S_H,T_H)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(S_PS_Q,T_QT_P)$ and the natural isomorphism $\delta:R_2\cong R_1$ from step 3. All hypotheses are now present. The lemma supplies a unique natural transformation $d:L_1\to L_2$, makes it an isomorphism, and gives exactly $T_H(d_M)\circ u_{1,M}=\delta_{S_PS_QM}\circ u_{2,M}$. Uniqueness among natural transformations implies the requested uniqueness among natural isomorphisms.

source.place: final pullback-composition sentence; uniqueness of left adjoints with the prescribed units (Stacks Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints)

proof.text:
Write $L_1=S_H$, $R_1=T_H$, $L_2=S_PS_Q$, $R_2=T_QT_P$ and let $\varepsilon_2$ be the counit of the composite adjunction. By the component formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], the conjugate of $d$ at an $A$-module $N$ is
$$d^c_N=R_1(\varepsilon_{2,N})\circ R_1(d_{R_2N})\circ u_{1,R_2N}.$$
Substitute the unit equation of step 4 at $R_2N$, then use naturality of $\delta$ at $\varepsilon_{2,N}$ and the right-adjoint triangle identity of the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]:
$$d^c_N=R_1(\varepsilon_{2,N})\circ\delta_{L_2R_2N}\circ u_{2,R_2N}=\delta_N\circ R_2(\varepsilon_{2,N})\circ u_{2,R_2N}=\delta_N.$$
The inverse clause of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] therefore gives $(d^{-1})^c=\delta^{-1}$. In every step only $c_M$ was inverted; the coefficient maps were used solely as monoid morphisms for restriction, so none of them has been assumed invertible.
